titleZh: 「There is every reason to believe that ...」表示「有充分理由相信」
titleEn: Using “There is every reason to believe that ...”

formula: There is every reason to believe that + complete clause

formulas.formula: There is every reason to believe that + complete clause

example: There is every reason to believe that the trend will continue.
exampleZh: 我們有充分理由相信，這個趨勢會持續下去。

examples.en: There is every reason to believe that the trend will continue.
examples.zh: 我們有充分理由相信，這個趨勢會持續下去。
examples.highlight: There is every reason to believe that the trend will continue.

meaning.zh: 本課練習目標句型：There is every reason to believe that + complete clause。

rules.zh: 使用 There is，不要使用 There are Reason 是單數名詞，因此必須使用 is。
rules.en: Use There is, not There are, because reason is singular. Correct: There is every reason to believe that the plan will work. Incorrect: There are every reasons to believe that the plan will work.
examples: Correct: There is every reason to believe that the plan will work.
Incorrect: There are every reasons to believe that the plan will work.

rules.zh: that 後面必須接完整子句 完整子句需要包含主語和動詞。
rules.en: Follow that with a complete clause containing a subject and verb. Correct: There is every reason to believe that the team will win. Incorrect: There is every reason to believe that the team’s victory.
examples: Correct: There is every reason to believe that the team will win.
Incorrect: There is every reason to believe that the team’s victory.

rules.zh: every reason 並非逐字表示「每一個理由」 在這個固定表達中，every reason 表示「非常充分的理由」或「有力的理據」。
rules.en: Every reason idiomatically means very strong or compelling grounds, not a literal count of every possible reason.

rules.zh: 這個句型表達強烈信心，但不是絕對肯定 它比以下句子更有信心： （有理由相信這個計劃會成功。） 但它沒有以下句子那麼絕對： （這個計劃肯定會成功。）
rules.en: The structure expresses strong confidence without absolute certainty. It is stronger than “There is reason to believe that the plan will work” but less absolute than “It is certain that the plan will work.”
examples: There is reason to believe that the plan will work.
It is certain that the plan will work.

rules.zh: that 子句可以包含否定意思 （我們有充分理由相信，不會再有進一步延誤。）
rules.en: The that-clause may be negative: There is every reason to believe that there will be no further delay.
examples: There is every reason to believe that there will be no further delay.

rules.zh: 本練習使用完整形式 日常口語中可以使用： 但本練習統一使用完整形式：
rules.en: Use the full form in this exercise. “There’s every reason to believe that ...” is possible in everyday speech, but the model answers consistently use “There is every reason to believe that ....”
examples: There’s every reason to believe that ...
There is every reason to believe that ...

benefits.zh: 表達強烈但審慎的信心 這個句型表示你有充分證據支持自己的判斷，但沒有把事情說成百分之百肯定。因此，它比直接 使用 definitely 或 certainly 更審慎。
benefits.en: It expresses strong but careful confidence. The structure shows that substantial evidence supports the judgement without presenting it as one hundred per cent certain, so it is more cautious than definitely or certainly.

benefits.zh: 清楚連接證據和結論 你可以先提出證據，再使用這個句型帶出合理結論，讓讀者清楚理解你的判斷從何而來。
benefits.en: It connects evidence with a conclusion. You can present the evidence first and then use this structure to introduce a reasonable conclusion, making the basis of the judgement clear.

benefits.zh: 比反覆使用 “I think” 更客觀 後者把重點放在證據和理據上，而不是只表達個人感覺。
benefits.en: It sounds more objective than “I think” because it focuses on evidence and reasoning rather than personal feeling. Instead of “I think the treatment is working”, write: There is every reason to believe that the treatment is working.

benefits.zh: 適合作文、報告和簡報 這個句型可以用來提出有根據的預測、分析研究結果、評估計劃，或根據現有資料作出判斷。
benefits.en: It is useful in essays, reports and presentations for making evidence-based predictions, analysing research findings, evaluating plans, or drawing judgements from available information.

benefits.zh: 幫助控制說法的肯定程度 這個句型比 may、might 或 perhaps 更有信心，但仍然保留合理的審慎態度。 Comparison 對比例子 （測試結果理想，所以我認為治療正在發揮作用。） （我們有充分理由相信治療正在發揮作用，因為測試結果理想。） 第二句更清楚地把證據和結論連接起來。
benefits.en: It helps control the strength of a claim. It expresses more confidence than may, might or perhaps while retaining reasonable caution. Compare: The test results are positive, so I think the treatment is working. There is every reason to believe that the treatment is working because the test results are positive. The second sentence connects the evidence and conclusion more clearly.
